title: Healthy Donor Controls for Immune Evaluation
description: Bioenergetic dysfunction is an archetypical finding in critical illness, particularly among patients with sepsis. A central feature of sepsis is the shift towards pathologic immunosuppression predisposing to secondary infections and ineffectual organ recovery. However, the extent to which metabolic abnormalities contribute to immune cell dysregulation in critically ill patients with and without sepsis remains unclear. To investigate this, we collected peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from medical and surgical ICU patients at Vanderbilt University Medical Center 48-72 hours after ICU admission, as well as community-matched healthy controls, with all studies conducted under IRB approval. We performed single cell RNA-sequencing using the Chromium Next GEM Single Cell 5' HT... (for more see dbGaP study page.)
